source_text.body:
Run Lighthouse SEO audits and fix a site with an agent
An agent using chrome-devtools-mcp ran Lighthouse on the author's site, applied fixes, and re-audited to reach 100 on Accessibility and SEO.
·
Jun 14, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The author connected Google's official chrome-devtools-mcp to a real Chrome and ran its lighthouse_audit tool against the seo-kreativ.de homepage. The audit covered the classic categories plus the new experimental Agentic Browsing category. The author then fixed the findings: button and text contrast, a discernible name for the logo link, re-enabled zoom, and label mismatches. After that came a repeat audit.
How it went
Accessibility rose from 89 to 100, SEO stayed at 100, and Agentic Browsing rose from 33% to 67%. The llms.txt check still fails because of a Yoast generation detail, which the author chose not to fix.
Worth knowing
This is a single test on one site. The security note says to avoid logged-in sessions and to use the --isolated option with a temporary profile.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Using chrome-devtools-mcp, run a Lighthouse audit on [my site URL] and list every Accessibility and SEO issue it finds. Fix the issues in my codebase at [project folder], then re-run the audit to confirm. Stop when Accessibility and SEO both score 100 or you've listed what's blocking it, and show me a summary of the changes before committing anything.
Original source: https://www.seo-kreativ.de/en/blog/seo-audits-with-ai-agents-chrome-devtools-mcp/
